The proposed solution contains an error in the dimension of the minimal nilpotent orbit in the orthogonal Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}_m$.

1. **Dimension of the minimal nilpotent orbit in $\mathfrak{so}_m$:**
   The dual Coxeter number of $\mathfrak{so}_m$ (for $m \ge 5$) is $h^\vee = m - 2$. The dimension of the minimal nilpotent orbit in any simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ is given by:
   $$\dim\left(\mathbb{O}_{\min}^{\mathfrak{g}}\right) = 2h^\vee - 2$$
   Applying this to $\mathfrak{so}_m$:
   $$\dim\left(\mathbb{O}_{\min}^{\mathfrak{so}_m}\right) = 2(m - 2) - 2 = 2m - 6$$
   The proposed solution incorrectly claims this dimension is $2m - 4$. (For example, in $\mathfrak{so}_5 \cong \mathfrak{sp}_4$, the minimal orbit has dimension $4$, whereas $2(5)-4 = 6$).

2. **Dimension check for $m = 2n + 1$:**
   If $m = 2n + 1$, the minimal nilpotent orbit in $\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}$ has dimension:
   $$2(2n + 1) - 6 = 4n - 4$$
   Performing a $\mathbb{C}^*$-Hamiltonian reduction lowers the complex dimension by $2$:
   $$\dim(\text{Reduction}) = (4n - 4) - 2 = 4n - 6$$
   However, the affine closure $\overline{T^*\mathbb{O}_n}^{\mathrm{aff}}$ has dimension $4n - 4$. Since $4n - 4 \ne 4n - 6$, the varieties cannot be isomorphic. 

Equating the correct dimensions gives $(2m - 6) - 2 = 4n - 4$, which yields $m = 2n + 2$, not $2n + 1$.

VERDICT: REJECT
